@nodejs/tsc @nodejs/readline this is ready for reviews.
What makes the PR semver-major?

> What makes the PR semver-major?

It adds a new core module (`readline/promises`) and with the refactoring to ES6 class, I think it's safer to land this in a semver-major.

Was the refactoring necessary to make the promise version?
This pull request is difficult to review because it does everything in one commit and moves a lot of code. That's also a problem for backporting conflicts.
The refactoring is necessary if we don't want the promise version to expose its internal methods and properties. I can certainly split this is in multiple commits to help the review process though.

(I'm responding to https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/37947#discussion_r621470666 in the main issue because I think it's relevant to everybody)

The goal of introducing promise-based version of our API is to _deprecate the callback version_: it must be functionally equivalent.

At the current state this PR it is not equivalent. Consider the following:

```js
// The errors bubble up naturally 
cursorTo(stream, 0, 1)
cursorTo(stream, 2, 3)
```

vs

```js
// Await is needed to catch errors
await cursorTo(stream, 0, 1)
await cursorTo(stream, 2, 3)
```

Those two API are not equivalent because the promise version waits for the chunk to be fully written before allowing the new command.

In reality, what would be needed to make them equivalent is:

```js
await Promise.all([
  await cursorTo(stream, 0, 1)
  await cursorTo(stream, 2, 3)
])
```

I think it's a far worse user experience that the callback API we aim to replace.

Why not pass the `cursorTo` error to the stream instead of rejecting the promise with it?

I think your example with:

```js
  cursorTo(stream, 0, 1).catch(reject);
  cursorTo(stream, 2, 3).catch(reject);
```

Shows Matteo's point of how problematic this API can be (since the second reject would be swallowed if the promise above it would be executed)

Oh right, it would actually something like that:
```js
await Promise.race([
  cursorTo(stream, 0, 1),
  Promise.resolve(),
]);
await Promise.race([
  cursorTo(stream, 2, 3),
  Promise.resolve(),
]);
```

I agree this looks like bad design, but em.. so would be synchronous throw IMHO.

> Why not pass the `cursorTo` error to the stream instead of rejecting the promise with it?

Note that we're talking about param validation error, so there might be no stream to pass them to. I'd prefer an option parameter to opt-in to that behavior, but if that's well documented, I'd be fine with that personally.

I think we should think of a _different_ APi and not a 1:1 port.

```js
const r = new Readline(stream)
await r.cursorTo(0, 1)
 .cursorTo(1, 2)
 .exec()
```

issue_context.title: Add Promises version of ReadLine
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
Not to my knowledge.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
I'd like to have access to a set of functions for the readline portion of Node in a similar style to `import fs from 'fs/promises'`. Having to wrap callback functions in promises is rather tedious. 

I'd like to know if this would be something I can work on. I want this for my own purposes and have the time to work on and implement this if possible.
comments: I agree it would make sense for Node.js to provide promise-based versions of `readline.clearLine`, `readline.clearScreenDown`, `readline.cursorTo`, and `readline.moveCursor`. `readline.Interface` is an `AsyncIterator`, which is already a promise API, but its methods (such as `question`) would deserve to have a Promise-based equivalent.
I would like to work on this. Is that alright?

> I would like to work on this. Is that alright?

That's fine by me, was going to get to this after doing some work on something else but if you're free go for it.
